title: Slice pullback comparison is induced by the ringed localization square
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a continuous functor defining a morphism $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ whose inverse image preserves finite limits, and let $R$ on $\mathcal D$ and $S$ on $\mathcal C$ be sheaves of commutative rings with a ring map $c:f^{-1}R\to S$. For $V\in\mathcal D$ put $U=u(V)$, give $\mathcal D/V$ and $\mathcal C/U$ the localized topologies and restricted rings [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and let $f_V$, the commutative ringed localization square and the ordinary module comparison $\sigma:(f_V)^*j_V^*\cong j_U^*f^*$ be those of [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. Use the unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with localization functor $q$, the exact derived restrictions $j_V^*,j_U^*$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction], the derived pullbacks $Lf^*,Lf_V^*$ computed on K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], and the derived adjunctions $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Lf_V^*\dashv R(f_V)_*$. Let $\beta:j_V^*Rf_*\cong R(f_V)_*j_U^*$ and $\theta:Lf_V^*j_V^*\cong j_U^*Lf^*$ be the canonical comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization]. Then for every K-flat complex $P$ of $R$-modules with flat terms, under the identifications $Lf^*(qP)\cong q(f^*P)$ and $Lf_V^*(q\,j_V^*P)\cong q((f_V)^*j_V^*P)$ (the restriction $j_V^*P$ is again K-flat with flat terms) and the termwise identifications $j_V^*(qP)=q(j_V^*P)$, $j_U^*(q f^*P)=q(j_U^*f^*P)$, the component $\theta_{qP}$ equals $q(\sigma_P)$. Consequently $\theta$ is the derived pullback comparison induced by the commutative ringed localization square, and $\beta$ is its exchange mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], that is, the base change map of this square.

proof.text: Restriction preserves K-flatness by lem-sfb-ringed-site-restriction-kflat and preserves flat terms by lem-weil-pbc-slice-restriction-flat. The localized set pullback preserves finite limits by lem-weil-pbc-slice-set-pullback-isIso. Apply lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-image-exists globally and locally to obtain presentations whose epsilon components are invertible on flat-term K-flat complexes. For either given presentation, Mathlib Functor.leftDerivedLift and isLeftDerivedFunctor_iff_isIso_leftDerivedLift identify it with the supplied presentation. The equation leftDerived_fac_app and cancellation of this invertible comparison transfer invertibility to the given epsilon.

Apply the unit equation of lem-weil-pbc-slice-module-pullback-isIso in each degree. The sectionwise direct-image comparison is the identity. Extensionality of complex morphisms gives that the ordinary local transpose of sigma_P is restriction of the global ordinary unit, followed by ringedSlicePushforwardComplexIso. Differentials are already respected by the real chain-map construction ringedSlicePullbackComplexMap.

Specialize the normalized field of the global RingedSliceDerivedImage to the identity of the actual pulled-back complex FP. The derived global unit followed by R(epsilon_P) is Q of the ordinary global unit followed by eta_FP. Compose the square unit identity with R_v(lambda_P), cancel lambda inverse against lambda, and obtain the local transpose of lambda_P as restriction of the global derived unit followed by beta.

Apply the local derived adjunction Hom equivalence to both sides of the representative equation. For the left side, the preceding unit equation, naturality of beta at epsilon_P, the normalized global unit, and hnormal at I=FP reduce its transpose to j_V(Q(unit_P)); cr_GP; Q(tau_FP); eta_local. Naturality of the restriction factorization cr at the ordinary unit moves cr to the front. For the right side, naturality of the Hom equivalence in its source, the local presentation normalized field, and the ordinary transpose identity give the identical expression. Functoriality of Q and associativity complete this equality. Injectivity of the local Hom equivalence proves the displayed equation, with every model and restriction comparison retained. No injectivity or K-injectivity hypothesis on FP is used.

The square counit field says that L_v(beta_M) followed by the local counit is lambda_RM followed by restriction of the global counit. Applying the local Hom equivalence yields the last assertion. Mathlib mateEquiv_counit gives the same inverse transpose for the component of mateEquiv(lambda). Injectivity of the inverse Hom equivalence and natural-transformation extensionality prove mateEquiv(lambda)=beta. This is the counit construction of the base-change exchange map in Stacks Tag 07A7. Resolution descent is unnecessary for these quantified conclusions.
